system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review — Project Kestrel.** The Seller’s package should not be accepted as drafted. The positions below are buyer negotiating targets, not assertions of agreed or “standard market” terms. The underlying SPA and DD documents have not been supplied for verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separately protected claim categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and available security; a 20% cap leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket; exclusions for specially protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with recovery from the first dollar once triggered; the proposed combination materially erodes recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notification within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, separate category deadlines and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Seek 36 months and reject blanket extension to all Claims**; latent problems may emerge after 18 months and other claims require different treatment. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title receive the general cap and deadline. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, all issued shares and freedom from encumbrances; no basket or de minimis. | **Seek a 100% purchase-price cap and seven-year notification period**, with fraud separately protected; defective title can undermine the entire acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is identified. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation claims, appropriately covering Seller-attributable conduct, and non-excludable rights. | **Exclude fraud from caps, thresholds, contractual time bars and remedy/reliance restrictions**, to the extent legally permissible; the Seller must not contractually shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; a frozen, indexed disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure and require specific warranty-linked disclosures**; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Actual adviser/Buyer knowledge and anything discoverable in the data room or public records bar claims. | Preferably no knowledge bar; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel, without deemed or imputed knowledge. | **Delete “discoverable” and blanket adviser attribution**; diligence access must not become an unrestricted defence to warranty liability. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence of associated conditions being satisfied. | An effective consent satisfying clauses 11.2–11.3, without unacceptable conditions, termination rights or adverse commercial changes. | **Make satisfactory consent and satisfaction of its conditions a Buyer-waivable condition precedent**, with a long-stop termination right; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout, repayment and effective release of all relevant security and guarantees at Completion, consistent with debt-free/cash-free pricing. | **Require a lender payout letter and controlled simultaneous discharge arrangements**, including necessary registrations; the Buyer should not acquire an encumbered business and depend on later Seller performance. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller economic responsibility for transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with correct payroll treatment. | **Quantify and expressly allocate these amounts through funds flow or a price deduction, backed by an indemnity and no double counting**; omission risks shifting Seller transaction costs to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** shown open, without payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective transfer of all relevant IP rights; protection against ownership gaps, infringement claims and remediation losses arising from the matter. | **Require payment evidence and an effective assignment before Completion, plus a broader specific indemnity outside general warranty limitations**; paying an invoice alone may not establish the required IP ownership. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, preservation of evidence, containment, legal assessment and required notifications, with Seller responsibility for pre-Completion incident exposure. | **Require a documented response plan and specific indemnity, supported by retention if warranted**; uncertainty does not establish a confirmed notifiable breach, but equally does not justify dismissing the risk. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Assessment together of timing, necessity, termination rights, accruals and post-Completion benefit; consent controls over material pre-Completion commitments. | **Verify before accepting the characterisation and allocate under agreed debt/working-capital rules where appropriate**; related commitments must be assessed together, but are not automatically debt-like. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend across all Claims. | Expressly separate regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price adjustments and fraud. | **Rewrite the application and precedence provisions, with express exclusions in every relevant clause**; negotiated protection is ineffective if an overarching clause silently cuts it down. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital and ownership, including transfers, allotments, options, convertibles, encumbrances and third-party rights. | **Obtain supporting corporate records, relevant searches, title warranties and complete transfer/release deliverables**; the share register is important evidence, not complete verification of clean title. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP positions treated as settled under the general regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with an appropriate assessment-based period and distinct cap; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection. | **Expressly reserve both as open**: negotiate tax survival through applicable assessment periods plus a buffer and IP protection proportionate to this analytics business; the general regime does not adequately address either exposure. |

**Immediate priorities:** secure effective Bluefen consent, simultaneous Riverlark discharge, verified Ironquay rights and an accurate bonus-inclusive funds flow. Known disclosed risks need affirmative contractual protection—not reliance on warranties that the disclosure may qualify.
=== END ADVICE ===
